picks.headline: Storytel launched AI-generated audiobook recaps in Finland without telling authors
picks.excerpt: Storytel's AI 'Recaps' summarise the last 5-15 minutes of an audiobook; Finnish author Suvi Auvinen and the Writers' Union object that authors weren't notified and AI summaries can distort works. Storytel says publishers got a month's notice and an opt-out. (Finnish-language article)
picks.rationale: A live AI feature from a major audiobook platform, plus a concrete consent dispute (the publisher opt-out versus authors never being told). It changes what authors should check in their audio contracts right away.
picks.framing_note: WRITER: explain what Recaps does (it summarises the last 5-15 minutes), then set out both sides: the author and union objections, and Storytel's publisher notice and opt-out. The source is in Finnish, so the enrichment pass must translate carefully and attribute quotes.

picks.headline: We Don't Want Shonen Jump AI Manga Translations
picks.excerpt: Shueisha appears to be surveying MANGA Plus readers on AI translation, a sign it is weighing machine-translated manga releases; the piece argues MT can't replace human localization.
picks.rationale: It suggests the biggest manga publisher is testing whether readers will accept AI-translated releases on MANGA Plus. This is a new signal, separate from the 09-12 Webtoon translation card.
picks.framing_note: WRITER: lead with the fact (the MANGA Plus reader survey on AI translation) and present the argument against machine translation as Siliconera's opinion. Do not say Shueisha has decided anything; it is only surveying.

picks.headline: 일본 헌책방 매출 5배 증가…AI 학습용으로 50톤이 미국행, 스캔 뒤 폐기
picks.excerpt: 일본 헌책방 매출이 최대 5배 늘었다. 2022년 이전 출간 도서를 톤 단위로 사들여 50톤 넘게 미국으로 수출, AI 학습용으로 스캔한 뒤 폐기하는 흐름이다.
picks.rationale: New, concrete data on book scanning for AI training: Japanese used-book sales up as much as fivefold and over 50 tonnes shipped to the US. Earlier cards covered Amazon's US warehouse; this is a new market and new numbers.
picks.framing_note: WRITER: lead with the numbers (up to 5x sales, 50+ tonnes, books from before 2022). You may mention the European Writers' Council condemnation of 'destructive scanning' (25 Sep) as context in one line; it was folded in as a within-pool duplicate.

picks.headline: "내가 바로 웹툰 주인공"⋯네이버웹툰 AI 캐릭터챗으로 만드는 새 이야기
picks.excerpt: 네이버웹툰의 AI 스토리챗 '바이어스(byUs)'가 출시 10주 만에 누적 대화 1400만건을 돌파. 작가가 승인·검수한 IP 설정 위에서 독자가 주인공이 돼 2차 서사를 만들고, 원작 조회수도 67% 늘었다.
picks.rationale: A shipping AI reading product with real traction: 14M conversations in 10 weeks and 67% more views of the original works. It is also a model where authors approve the settings the AI works from. This is a positive, product-side story that balances the controversy items.
picks.framing_note: WRITER: lead with the numbers and how it works (author-approved IP settings, reader as the protagonist). Attribute the metrics to Naver Webtoon.

picks.headline: Novelist accused of using AI to write book removed from French prize list
picks.excerpt: Thélyson Orélien's debut was dropped from the Prix Goncourt list after AI-authorship claims spread on social media.
picks.rationale: A new development, not a repeat: the 09-24 Bookseller card covered only the accusation, with both publishers backing the author. This card is about the first real consequence, removal from the Goncourt list. It is a precedent for how prizes handle AI-authorship claims.
picks.framing_note: WRITER: the headline and body must be about the removal from the Prix Goncourt list, not a re-telling of the accusation. Refer to the earlier accusation in one clause at most. The claims are still unproven, so attribute them and do not state that AI was used.
